notesStmt.note: This manuscript most likely dates to the days just prior to the poem's initial publication.

"Ah, Not This Granite Dead and Cold" was originally published as in the Philadelphia Press on February 22, 1885. Whitman later made minor revisions and republished the poem under the title "Washington's Monument, February, 1885" in November Boughs (1888) and in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891–1892).

lg.head: Ah, not this that granite dead and cold!
lg.l: Ah, not this that granite dead and cold!

Far far from its base and shaft expanding—the
round zones circling, comprehending,

No ‸limited lurid fame exceptional ‸od for thee,, ¶nNor monstrous disproportional in-
tellectintellect
, nor conquest's domination

Thou Washington art all the world's, ‸humanitys the continents ‸entire——not
yours alone, America,

Europe's as well, in every land part, in castle or in castle of lord, or laborer's cot—
‸or from north, or sultry south— the Arab's in his tent—the African's,

Old Asia's there with venerable smile seated
amid her ruins,

(Greets the antique the hero new? 'tis but the
same—the undying indomitable heart and arm—the
heir legitimate, —the same unbroken —proofs of the never broken line

Courage, alertness, pateience, hope, the same—e'en
in defeat defeated not, the same;)

Where'erever ‸sails a ship, sails, or house is built on land,
or night or day,

Through teeming cities' streets, indoors or out,
factories or farms,

Now or to come or past—wherever patriot
wills existed or exist

Wherever Freedom, poised by Toleration, swayed
by Law,—in them, from them,

l.del: Rising or risen, there's thy true monument,

lg.l: Rises or stands or is rising thy true monument.
